note: Vol. I No. 41. The town is on page 3. Columns 2 and 5 are the Tesseract fallback and carry the month's new matter unbroken — the Chicago Bakery, Pierce & French, Mathias Mason & Co., the Carver and Bradford notices — while columns 1, 3, 4 and 6 are the Vision reading, where the segmenter alternates two physical columns line by line. Column 5 sets TWO printed columns side by side on one line, so its claims use `locator.spans` to quote the left one and leave the right where it stands.

claims.notes: A PLACEMENT THAT DOES NOT FIT THE PLAT, recorded as printed and flagged rather than quietly repaired. The canal commissioners' 1830 plat has no MAIN STREET, so this anchor cannot be laid down on the town's ground as it stands; the Tremont House is a Chicago house and the dateline reads Chicago, 26 November 1833, so the advertisement is not obviously another town's. The possibilities — that Main-street is a name in local use for a platted street, that the dateline and the address belong to different towns, or that the segmenter has fused two advertisements — are not decidable from this witness and NONE of them is chosen here. The placement is kept `relative` on the Tremont House with the street recorded as the paper prints it, and this note is the flag for whoever tries to place it.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. EVERY LINE OF THIS COLUMN IS INSIDE AN UNCERTAINTY MARK, the transcription's own, and they are quoted with the marks rather than stripped. The display line is lost.
